newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares set third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares set third straight record close.

text.p: 1505 GMT - Swiss shares rebounded from opening losses to post a third straight record high at the end of a volatile session. Prices were drawn up by gains in a few financial stocks such as Zurich, Credit Suisse and SBC.
"We all have the impression that the market is high, but we end up going even higher," one dealer said, adding, "We don't understand it anymore."
The favourable environment and ample liquidity made further gains possible although nervousness was increasing, he added.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closed 30.4 points, or 0.54 percent, higher at 5,700.3.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 15.62 points, or 0.44 percent, to 3,593.51.
Bourse volume stood at 2.57 billion Swiss francs.
"The bourse favourites change by the day," one trader noted, adding that financials were favoured today while recent high-flyers such as Nestle, Novartis and Roche were neglected.
* Zurich Group continued to be bolstered by news of its imminent purchase of U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark.
The stock rose 11 francs to 600, reflecting the market's positive view of the deal.
* Among banks, SBC and Credit Suisse jumped 19 francs to 395.50 and seven francs to 196.0. Dealers said the gains were the result of large buy orders.
One dealer cited old rumours the two banks may merge some back office activities. "But I can hardly bear to hear these rumours again," he added.
* ABB also was among the day's winners, climbing 26 francs to 2,220.
* Novartis registered shares consolidated recent gains, giving up four francs to 2,363. Roche also lost ground.
* On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), options in Credit Suisse and SBC were in the limelight.
Total options volume was at 112,617 with a call/put ratio of 1.65 to one.
On the futures side, 4,385 SMI futures were traded. The July SMI futures was up 22.0 points to 5,702.0.
